note: What each lap claimed the ETA would become, recorded before the work. outcome is filled in later from state/eta-history.json. A claim written afterwards is not a prediction, so rows are appended by scripts/eta-gate.mjs and not by hand.

claims.mechanism: The #1 candidate is blocked on naming where the CORRECTED buyer class gathers. state/portfolio.json the_priced_artifact.who_it_actually_addresses records that task .k asked about developers buying source code, while the product description addresses shops, cafes, salons, streamers and campaign pages. .k's questions 1 and 4 are therefore aimed off-target and its venue answer is for the wrong crowd. This lap re-asks the venue and rule questions against the class the description actually names. It cannot itself make the ETA finite, so it is claimed as a prerequisite: it produces the venue+rule evidence that a direct route claim would have to rest on. Cost falls on the ChatGPT pool, not the weekly quota.

state/owner-requests.json lists as unverified whether the free demo is reachable by a stranger: claude.ai artifacts are private by default, and the owner's own list showing it proves nothing about a third party. codex/outbox/2026-08-09.i.md found that every fast first-sale case posted something the reader could try immediately, so a dead demo link removes the announcement's strongest element. This is not re-preparing the request — the request is written and the read_this_before_acting note forbids rewriting it. It closes a gap the request itself names, and it is work this side can do with no owner action. Prerequisite because verifying a link cannot make the ETA finite.

codex/outbox/2026-08-09.l.md is the first survey to come back 落ちる about the PRODUCT rather than about a candidate shape. Every confirmed purchase by the class the description addresses was a monthly SaaS carrying an admin panel, hosting and setup help; no buy-once config-file kit purchase was found at all. Price is not the problem — USD 25 is under one month of every comparable. This has to reach the picker as a constraint, because eta.json is generated and a finding written anywhere else is not read. It forces a branch: re-aim the description at the class whose form already matches (developers/agencies, where the itch route is already prepared), or change the form to hosted. Recording it cannot itself make the ETA finite, so it is prerequisite — and it is the third, which closes the prerequisite budget and forces the next lap to make a direct claim. That is the intended behaviour, not a problem to route around.

Abandon the route 'sell a buy-once, self-installed config-file kit to shops, salons and streamers'. codex/outbox/2026-08-09.l.md found zero confirmed purchases of that form by that class, and every confirmed purchase by that class was an operated monthly service. Branch A keeps the form, which .k measured as selling (itch Game Assets, 38 clicker listings among top sellers, USD 25 inside the observed band), and changes the addressee to people who build their own idle/clicker game. The live Gumroad listing is the route: its title, body and licence paragraph all name the refuted class, so every downstream distribution act inherits the mismatch. Re-aiming the listing is what makes the pending itch request coherent, since itch Game Assets is a branch-A venue. No ETA number can be claimed to move yet because no channel feeds the listing, which is precisely why this is a route change and not a direct claim.

The Claude weekly pool is the binding resource (11.40% discretionary against a 26.60% reservation for automations nobody has measured) while the Codex pool sits unused. Every kind of work that turns out to be delegable moves off the binding constraint, which is arithmetically the same as halving lap cost but gives nothing up. state/constraints.json codex_lane_capability_range_unmapped is measured_at null: all ten tasks sent to that lane were outside research, which is the history of our orders and not the range of the lane. Task .m asks for five small artifacts and is judged on whether they arrive, because a self-report is not a measurement. This lap dispatches it and records what actually came back. It cannot itself make the ETA finite, so it is claimed as groundwork - the first since the route_change reset the run.

The live Gumroad product carries tags=[] and category=other (measured via GET /v2/products this lap). Gumroad Discover ranks and browses by tag and taxonomy, so an untagged product in 'other' is absent from the only venue this account can reach with zero standing and zero owner actions. Populating tags and taxonomy is the 'substitute breadth' half of this constraint's two_ways_it_lifts, which the constraint records as never tried. It does not shorten a measured ETA on its own - no channel has a derivable rate yet - so it is admitted as prerequisite, not direct.

Gumroad Discover browse is a visual grid of tiles. The product entered that index yesterday-lap via eight tags but serves covers:[], main_cover_id:null, thumbnail_url:null, preview_url:null, so it presents a blank tile to everyone the index shows it to. The single unmeasured thing is OUR side: whether the v2 API can set a cover at all. scripts/render-cover.mjs already produces the image locally with no network, so settling the upload question either automates the fix outright or reduces the owner request to uploading a file we made. RUNBOOK gate 1 forbids raising the owner request before the automation has actually been attempted, so this measurement is the precondition for both branches. Claims no day movement: every channel is still non-derivable, so a direct claim would be invented.

Abandon the route this loop has spent its laps on - making ONE storefront findable on its own (copy, then tags, then cover, then category) - and take the one the evidence names. zerobase refuted.not_refuted for honest_post_where_buyers_gather says posting into a buyer community DOES reach a first buyer and is by far the fastest route on record, three cases at 0-1 days from publish to first revenue. What fell was only its 'exactly one post from a standing start' shape, and what_it_leaves names the surviving term precisely: the blocker is STANDING, and BREADTH SUBSTITUTES FOR IT - Invoker had zero audience, both calendar dates, a first sale on day zero, and hit three venues at once. no_standing_where_buyers_gather already lists 'substitute breadth (a single bounded act, never tried)' as one of its two lift mechanisms; this adopts that mechanism explicitly. Two preconditions that were missing at 10:45 are now measured as present: the survey found no case where a bare announcement sufficed and every fast case posted a finished artifact the reader could try immediately, and as of today the priced kit is decidably public (200/27465 bytes with the product name served, against a fabricated-permalink 404/900 control). The incumbent route is not deleted - its Discover prediction still judges 2026-08-13 on its own - it just stops receiving laps.

The route adopted at 3555e97 needs a link a stranger can try in one click, and portfolio.json records the free demo's public reachability as UNDECIDABLE from here, naming the deciding instrument as 'a JavaScript-executing client carrying no claude.ai session' and citing playwright_cannot_reach_external as the reason we lack one. That constraint was measured 2026-08-08 as ERR_CONNECTION_RESET while curl succeeded in the same session - which is the exact signature of a browser not using this environment's HTTPS proxy, and nothing in the evidence says the proxy was ever passed to Chromium. If the recheck lifts it, planned ETA moves because both owner actions currently on the board become automatable: the itch page (form-only, owner_actions 1, request pending and unanswered) and the Gumroad cover upload (API proven incapable at 6dd65e2, so an owner upload is the only remaining path). If it does not lift, the free demo is decidably untryable from here and the venue post must be built around the priced page or a self-hosted build instead - which changes what the next lap writes. Either outcome changes the next act; this lap claims no ETA number of its own, which is why it is prerequisite.

The codex lane is the only instrument that can see the outside world, and the chosen route (post where buyers already are) is blocked on its answer. Measured: all 10 codex-inbox runs ever were workflow_dispatch; the daily cron has delivered zero. So an external answer arrives only when a lap happens to have MCP available, and RUNBOOK 0 records that MCP presence varies per lap. Raising the cron to hourly removes that dependency, so every future external question costs at most one hour of latency instead of one lap-with-MCP. It does not create revenue, so both ETA figures stay inf; it shortens the wait on every step of the route that does.

Task .o came back and it measures the adopted route rather than describing it: of three venues with rules quoted verbatim, zero are postable today from a standing start. r/gamedev forbids paid assets by written rule and permits free ones only when not locked behind signup; itch.io Release Announcements imposes no karma or account-age threshold and has a live dated slot (an asset pack on 2026-08-09) but requires an itch.io project page we do not have; GameDev.net's eligibility could not be established from public rules so it does not count as postable. That does not move a days figure - both stay inf - but it changes which candidate is next, which is what this constraint's fields drive. Two things get recorded where compute-eta reads them: the artifact bar stops being an inference from case studies and becomes a quoted venue rule, and the pending itch owner request stops being storefront tuning and becomes the precondition of the only venue that permits this product with a proven live slot.

Breadth has now been measured twice and returned the same answer: 6 venues surveyed across .o and .p, 0 postable today, and in the second batch all three failed on the SAME term - eligibility that cannot be established from public rules, because platforms do not publish those numbers. That is a finding about the method, not about venues, so a seventh survey buys nothing. The route changes from breadth-across-venues to one venue all-in: itch.io Release Announcements is the only surveyed venue that quotes permission for paid assets, states its eligibility as explicitly none, and shows a dated live slot. Its blocker is a single owner action that is already written and pending. So laps stop looking for alternatives and start removing every remaining reason that action can fail - beginning with the image the venue rules require in so many words.

The Gumroad product carries eight Discover tags and a blank tile: covers[], main_cover_id null, thumbnail_url null. Discover BROWSE is a grid of tiles, so every impression the tags now earn renders as an empty square. The v2 API was measured to have no cover route (probe-gumroad-cover.mjs: 404 byte-identical to a nonexistent path, PUT cover_url accepted-and-ignored exactly like a fake parameter), so the only remaining route is one owner upload. This lap does not claim days: it renders the 1280x720 cover here with Chromium and writes the paste-ready request, which is the pair state/constraints.json listing_has_no_cover_image.owner_action_note names as the condition for owner_request_prepared to flip true. Without the rendered file the request would ask the owner to make an image, which RUNBOOK gate 4 forbids.

The one door left points at a buyer class this repository already measured as refuted. codex/outbox/2026-08-09.l.md found zero buy-once kit purchases by shops, cafes, salons and streamers — every confirmed purchase by that class was an operated monthly service with an admin panel. assets/listing/gumroad.ja.json acted on that: branch A rewrote the Gumroad copy to address someone who builds and publishes their own game, and put 自社ブランド and 店舗サイト on a forbidden list a test enforces. The pending itch request never got that correction. Its page title, short description, body and announcement post all address the refuted class, in the venue whose market is Game Assets and whose board is for creators announcing their own work. So the route change was applied to the storefront nobody arrives at and not to the one venue that is left. This lap does not claim days: it makes the two surfaces address the same reader, and the reader is the measured one.

Every venue found so far is blocked on something outside this loop: itch needs an owner form, and the paid form is forbidden outright by the one large developer community whose rules were quoted. That same sentence permits FREE assets not locked behind a signup, which is the only door measured open that needs no owner action at all. It has never been scoped, and the reason recorded was that the kit source is not in this repository so there is nothing here to make free. That reason is about the KIT, not about the door: a small original demo written from scratch would also open it. Task .m already measured that the lane writes a JavaScript module with a node:test suite, and the lane itself proposed a dependency-free single-file HTML idle demo unprompted. So this lap scopes the door as a constraint with its measured facts and commissions the artifact on the Codex quota, which is 100 percent unused while ours is at 35. No days are claimed: what is produced is the thing a route change would need to exist before it can be gated as one.

Adopt the free-artifact route by writing down the rule that DEFINES it, in a machine rather than in a handoff note. r/gamedev permits free assets and forbids promoting paid ones in the same sentence, so the demo the lane is building opens the door only for as long as it carries no promotional link and no signup wall. That rule currently exists in exactly one place: prose in state/continue.json, which is rewritten every lap. The measured failure mode of this repository is that a decision survives only on surfaces with a reader, so the artifact will arrive and some lap will add a buy-the-full-kit line to it, and the door closes without anybody noticing it was open. This lap gives the rule a reader before the artifact exists. No ETA improvement is claimed: it removes a way the route can be destroyed, which is not the same as moving a number, and route_change is admitted on the cap rather than on a claim.

The route just adopted depends on an account nobody has established exists. Six venue surveys asked whether venues would permit us and never asked whether we can post at all, and the two facts sit on opposite sides of the file: state/itch.json returns HTTP 200 with a username, so an itch account is MEASURED, while nothing anywhere records a Reddit account. So the venue with an explicitly-none eligibility threshold and a confirmed account is the one waiting on a pending owner request, and the venue the loop just changed route toward is the one whose account is unverified. Nothing reports that asymmetry, so the next lap ranks the two as if they were alike. Make account existence a declared per-venue field that a machine refuses to leave blank, so a venue cannot be counted as a route on the strength of its rules alone. No ETA improvement claimed: it prices a route correctly rather than shortening one.

postable_today is the field that decides whether a venue is a live route, and the sweep found no line of code reads it (three independent observations: key-name sweep across scripts/tests/.github, grep outside state/, and reading venue-readiness.mjs which consumes the same rows and never mentions it). venues_postable_today_from_a_standing_start:0 is the count that closed the breadth route and drove a route_change, and it is hand-written with no reader. So when the pending itch owner action lands, itch.io becomes postable and nothing will notice: the count stays 0 and the route stays closed until a human happens to re-read the prose. This gives the field a reader that derives it from the account evidence AND the venue's own blocker as data, and fails when the stored value disagrees. It does not claim days; it stops the one distribution decision the loop has left from silently freezing shut.

Task .q delivered the original free demo the free-artifact route was waiting on, and codex/outbox/2026-08-09.q.md is the artifact's only home — an outbox file nothing serves and no venue can link. Installing it at assets/free-demo/index.html and running it through check-free-artifact.mjs is what converts a lane answer into the repository's own artifact, and it is the exact blocker r/gamedev's row names: promoting paid assets is forbidden and a free unwalled artifact is permitted in the same sentence. It buys no days, because postable then turns UNKNOWN rather than true — the Reddit account has never been established, which is the point my previous lap wired in. That is the honest after: one of the route's two blockers clears and the other becomes the binding one, named by a machine rather than by a sentence.

Abandoning the premise the route was adopted on, not a parameter of it. free_artifact_door was taken because r/gamedev is the one venue whose door opens with NO owner action. Measured today, that premise is false twice: no Reddit account has ever been established (owner fact, and reddit returns 403 from here so it cannot be looked up), and the venue needs a LINK to something tryable while nothing in this repository gives assets/free-demo/index.html a public home — a grep across state/ for hosting, pages, reachability and public URL finds only a sentence about the kit's source files, which is a different question. itch_no_write_api settles where the host comes from: butler pushes builds to an EXISTING page and has no page-creation command. So the free artifact is not an alternative to the owner; it is cargo that needs a host, and the host is an owner action. Both surviving venues now converge on the same single pending request. The route changes from 'a free artifact bypasses the owner' to 'one owner action unblocks both venues, and the demo is what makes it worth taking'.
